Manage is the manager's side of agent: one view of who is running, where,
on what model, with how much context and how many tokens, and the commands
that keep the data in hand. The manager GUI (agent-manager) draws "agent
manage view --json" and runs these commands; they work without it.

Nothing here is a second record. The view is read from this store and the
harnesses' transcripts each time it is asked for. The store keeps two
things for it: which sessions a person stopped tracking, and a cache of
each transcript's token count (rebuilt from the transcript when missing).

  view       the view, for a person or as JSON
  untrack    stop tracking sessions (the transcripts stay)
  track      track them again
  backup     copy the database to backups/
  prune      delete old records of finished things

Usage:
  agent manage [flags]
  agent manage [command]

Examples:
  agent manage view
  agent manage view --json --usage-budget 2s
  agent manage untrack --state ended,dormant --older-than 30d --dry-run
  agent manage backup
  agent manage prune --older-than 30d --dry-run

Available Commands:
  view        Show agents, sessions, tokens, friction, history and data for this host and its peers
  untrack     Stop tracking sessions: agent manage leaves them out (their transcripts stay)
  track       Track untracked sessions again
  backup      Copy this host's database to backups/
  prune       Delete old records of finished things: history, events, departed agents' runs and logs

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for manage

Global Flags:
      --backend string          Backend for spawn or adopt: claude, aider, agy, or shell (spawn requires it or --backend-config; adopt auto-detects)
      --backend-config string   JSON file defining a custom backend (or app settings); pass it again to status/wait/watch for agents spawned with it
  -q, --quiet                   Don't print hints (results and errors still print)
      --termd-ns string         g3d-termd namespace (default: agents; never default or wall)

Use "agent manage [command] --help" for more information about a command.
